title: What is the longest jump that lands on both treasures?
description: A number line shows the Jump Jackpot game with treasures on fourteen and thirty. The jump sizes that land on each treasure are listed, and the longest size on both lists is picked. The same steps then run for treasures on seven and eleven. Keeko's doubt, the jump as long as the bigger treasure, is tested on the line.
teaching_notes: One idea: a jump size lands on a treasure only if it is a factor of that number, so the longest jump for two treasures is their largest common factor. Watch for students who pick the bigger treasure number as the jump.

source: Treasures are on 14 and 30. Find the longest jump from 0 tha
video_script.why: The child knows the Jump Jackpot game and now links a landing jump to a factor of the treasure number.
video_script.substitution: Jumps from zero land on the multiples of the jump size, so a jump lands on a treasure exactly when its size is a factor of the treasure number.
video_script.anchor: A number line from zero with treasures on fourteen and thirty, and a jumper who picks one jump size.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the jump of thirty is longest because thirty is the bigger treasure. A jump of thirty from zero flies past fourteen and never lands on it.
video_script.payoff_line: The longest jump is two for the first pair, and one for the second pair.

final_answer.spoken: two for fourteen and thirty, and one for seven and eleven

names.{{NAME_5}}: places treasures on numbers in the Jump Jackpot game
names.{{NAME_2}}: chooses a jump size in the Jump Jackpot game

maths_rules: A jump of size s from 0 lands on s, 2s, 3s, ...; it lands on N exactly when s divides N.
Jump sizes landing on 14: 1 x 14, 2 x 7, so 1, 2, 7, 14.
Common sizes for 14 and 30: 1, 2. Longest is 2.
Jump sizes landing on 7: 1, 7. Jump sizes landing on 11: 1, 11. Common: 1. Longest is 1.
Slip: a jump of 30 lands on 30 but flies past 14, since 30 is not a factor of 14.
video_script.design: One idea: the jump size is a common factor of both treasure numbers, and the longest is the largest. Assumes factor lists. Wrong idea: the jump equals the bigger treasure. The number line stays all video.

narration: <bookmark mark='pairs'/>Step one, list the factors of fourteen, because each jump size must divide it. Fourteen is one times fourteen and two times seven.
<bookmark mark='list'/>The jump sizes are one, two, seven and fourteen.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: jump sizes landing on 30: 1 x 30, 2 x 15, 3 x 10, 5 x 6, so 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30

marks.pairs: The pairs that make thirty are written
marks.list: The jump sizes for thirty are listed

narration: <bookmark mark='pairs'/>Step two, list the factors of thirty in the same way. Thirty is one times thirty, two times fifteen, three times ten and five times six.
<bookmark mark='list'/>The jump sizes are one, two, three, five, six, ten, fifteen and thirty.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: common sizes 1, 2; the longest is 2

marks.longest: The larger circled size is underlined

beats.colours: the shared numbers in one colour
narration: <bookmark mark='both'/>Step three, pick the sizes on both lists, because the jump must land on both treasures. They are one and two.
<bookmark mark='longest'/>The longest of them is two.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: sizes landing on 7: 1, 7; sizes landing on 11: 1, 11

marks.seven: The jump sizes for seven are listed
marks.eleven: The jump sizes for eleven are listed

narration: <bookmark mark='seven'/>Step four, list the factors for the second pair. Seven is one times seven, so its sizes are one and seven.
<bookmark mark='eleven'/>Eleven is one times eleven, so its sizes are one and eleven.

beats.on_screen: Step 5: the only size on both lists is 1

marks.both: The only size on both lists is circled

beats.colours: the shared number in one colour
narration: <bookmark mark='both'/>Step five, look for the sizes on both lists. Only one is on both, because seven and eleven share no other factor.

beats.colours: the answer in the highlight colour
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The longest jump is two for the first pair, and one for the second pair.
